title: A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree
coverage: Read all seven sections in full. Section 2 (local): checked the normalization lemma's valuations (v_p of coefficient j=m_p is 0, and of j>m_p is at least u_p(j-m_p)-u'_p >= 1), integrality of g, and r+D_0n >= 1. Checked the family identity h_l(Dx-i)=lambda(D)h_{lD}(x) through r_{lD} ≡ r_l mod l and complete multiplicativity, the coefficient bound O(a_l), and preservation of the centered leading valuation. For the complete-sum lemma, checked Weyl differencing mod p, the j>=2 stationary-phase count via Lagrange interpolation ((k-1)(v-1)<n), and n>=j/3. Also checked the small-prime derivative bound via the Vandermonde adjugate, the Hensel-type lifting lemma (E>=2s+1), and the Fourier positivity of zero-sum length-L cycles (4δL>2). Section 3 (tuples): checked the Fourier bound on W, directedness (no 2-cycles since 2(t+1)>w-s), cycle support, the marked/unmarked pairing inequality, the threshold bookkeeping, the covariance W_{lD}(y)=W_l(lambda(D)y), and conditional mixing. Section 4 (lifts): checked the fold/Holder argument, the seminorm transport, the large-denominator orthogonality, the Gram-matrix row-sum constants in the moment bound, and the specialization factor q_B. Section 5 (kernel): checked the minor-arc Weyl bound (q' >= N^{η/2}, the three-term bound, 5ν), the Fourier l^1 norms of ρ_D and B_u, the major-arc errors against N^{-βγ/4}, the D-part factor χ_D through the lifting class, and the identities a+b=Γ_p (j=1) and 0 (j>=2). Also checked the q_1>H bound using 3<=p^{γ/2}, and the bilinear identity with signs and the ordering requirement. Section 6 (transfer): checked the progression partition and the inheritance of avoidance, the Fourier identity (28), and the cutoff change H→Q'. In the cancellation step, checked admissibility of a'_2-a'_1 at primes in B via the μ° cycle support, the exponent arithmetic, and the same-interval estimate. Section 7: checked the inclusion–exclusion expansion, Σ q_B η_B <= 1/4, the trial-bound calculation D_B^s and M_0^s(1-3ρ*/4), the l^b device for l>N^ζ, the strong induction, and the final transfer back to h through residue classes mod M. Also traced the degree-only dependence of P_1, E_p, L, t, d, P, M_0, ρ*, a_0. Spot-checks only; no independent symbolic computation was needed beyond the arithmetic checks.
main_claim: For each k>=2 there is c_k>0 such that for every intersective h of degree k with positive leading coefficient, any A ⊆ [N] with (A-A)∩h(N_+) ⊆ {0} has |A| <= C_h N^{1-c_k}. The proof first normalizes to g(x)=h(r+D_0x)/M so that the first nonzero Taylor coefficient at each chosen root is a p-adic unit. It then uses the Lucier auxiliary family h_l, which is covariant under progressions. On top of that it builds directed, weighted, reflection-positive tuple laws that transform exactly between h_l and h_{lD}, and a signed kernel on values of h_l whose Fourier transform matches the pair multipliers. Combining these gives the recurrence Y_l(N) <= C l^b N^{-a}, and every structural parameter is shown to depend only on k.
sibling_notes: This paper is a companion to the square-difference power-saving paper (family 182, rank 263, also no_gap_found). It reuses that paper's tuple-law, signed-Holder, lift-moment and induction architecture. The new parts are: the local normalization (U); the directed regular-fiber weights W, which need no negation symmetry; the covariance μ_{l,p} → μ_{lD,p}, which replaces dilation invariance; the polynomial kernel with derivative weights F'(m)/N and admissible argument classes; and the l^{b} factor in the induction to handle l>N^ζ at successor scales. All of these checked out.
